criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Primary mission (coral reef ocean monitoring with fluid lensing), rationale (bleaching, acidification), single satellite justification, and users (CSIRO, BOM, university/government operator) all clearly addressed with references.

evidence.quote: fluid lensing has been used in combination with AI analysis to detect colour/tone changes
only one satellite is required. This also just allows for simplicity in communications
would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: All main body requirements covered: launch site/vehicle with trade, SSO 600km orbit with calculated inclination and COE table, RAAN precession, maneuvers noted as EOL only, ground station selected with polar advantage, STK access report and ground tracks show contact frequency/duration, 5-year duration and drag-sail EOL.

evidence.quote: proposed satellite will thus use the Vega E rocket as a launch vehicle – launched from the Guiana Space Centre Spaceport
altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 97.7924° for the satellite to remain sun-synchronous
Tasmanian facility is selected – the Mount Pleasant Radio Observatory
An average contact duration of almost ten minutes was achieved, in addition to the already frequent amount of passes

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Conclusion synthesizes launch, orbit, ground station and EOL decisions from evidence and notes risk of Vega E availability with fallback to Vega C, appropriate for design.

evidence.quote: A specific launch vehicle – the Vega E – has been selected although it has not been built yet
A polar sun-synchronous orbit allows for consistent illumination of the oceans while maintaining a constant sun angle

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear report structure with executive summary, introduction, main body, conclusion, bibliography. Writing generally readable. Figures present but not all numbered/titled per spec, and Wikipedia cited as source contrary to task guidance.

evidence.quote: This report outlines the intended designs and procedures involved in the construction of a Earth observation satellite

technical_issues.issue: RAAN initial value statement linking RAAN 27.33 deg directly to launch facility latitude is oversimplified; RAAN depends on launch time/day, though value is plausible for Feb 2025 epoch.

STK access table contains duplicate entry for 5 Feb 13:00:32 and typo in start time 3 Feb vs 4 Feb for access 6, indicating table formatting/OCR artefact but does not affect mean duration ~580s conclusion.

overall: Comprehensive reef-monitoring SSO mission with solid STK evidence, correct altitude/inclination trade, appropriate ground station choice and EOL drag sail. Some presentation and referencing weaknesses.

feedback.summary: You delivered a comprehensive reef-monitoring SSO mission with strong STK evidence and clear rationale. Introduction and main body cover all required items with good trades. Conclusion ties decisions together. Writing is readable and structured, but figure numbering/titling and referencing need work to reach Accomplished for presentation.
next_steps: Add numbered titles and in-text callouts for all figures/tables (e.g., Image 3 ground track) and ensure consistent formatting to meet Accomplished presentation.
Replace Wikipedia citations with primary/peer-reviewed sources and ensure every in-text citation matches bibliography per task guidance.
In Orbit section, clarify how RAAN was selected relative to launch date/time and epoch, and double-check access tables for consistency.

criteria.C1: You did well: clear primary mission (fluid lensing for reef monitoring), strong rationale (bleaching/acidification), single-satellite justification, and users (CSIRO, BOM). To maintain Accomplished, deepen literature referencing for need and users.
criteria.C2: You covered all main body items: Vega E from Guiana Space Centre with trade, 600km SSO at 97.7924 deg with COE table, EOL-only maneuvers, Mount Pleasant ground station with polar advantage, and 580s average access. Keep strong STK evidence with screenshots.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion synthesises launch, SSO orbit, ground station and drag-sail EOL from evidence and notes Vega E risk with Vega C fallback. For higher Accomplished, explicitly link each conclusion to STK/hand-calc results.
criteria.C4: Structure is clear with Executive Summary and headings, writing readable. To reach Accomplished, number/title all figures (e.g., Image 3), reference them in text, and replace Wikipedia link in Bibliography with authoritative sources.
